Find and enquireStandard3–4 weeks

Safe enquiry routing for clinics and labs

Incoming WhatsApp and website messages are sorted by intent. Fees, timings, check-up packages, test preparation and directions are answered from approved content; symptoms, result questions and complaints go to the right staff member, and emergencies get an immediate instruction.

Clinics & day-care centres · Diagnostics & pathology labs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Small teams cannot answer every message quickly, and generic chatbots either frustrate patients or, worse, attempt medical advice. Enquiries left unanswered often book elsewhere, while messages that describe symptoms need a qualified person, not a template.

Trigger

A patient sends a WhatsApp message to the clinic or lab number, or submits the website enquiry form.

How it runs

  • Open a conversation linked to the CRM contact, creating it if new; replies inside the 24-hour service window need no template, and later follow-ups use approved templates only for patients who opted in.
  • Screen each message first against the emergency word list agreed with the clinical lead; on a match, reply at once with the facility's emergency number and 112 and alert the duty staff.
  • Classify the remaining text into intents such as fees, timings, check-up packages, test preparation, booking, report status, symptom or complaint, with a confidence score.
  • Answer administrative intents only from the approved FAQ, rate card or test master, citing the entry used; low-confidence drafts are not sent.
  • Hand symptom, medicine and result questions to the nurse or lab medical staff queue with a conversation summary, and tell the patient who will reply and when.
  • Log intent, handoff reason and response times for a weekly review of wording and routing rules.

Human checkpoint

The clinic nurse or the lab's medical officer answers every symptom, medicine or result question; front-office staff take complaints and anything the model is unsure about. The clinical lead approves the emergency word list and the FAQ before go-live.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • Clinic EMR or LIS test master
  • Approved rate card and FAQ
  • CRM contact records

Data & consent

Uses message text, phone number and name only; symptom details stay in the conversation for the clinical team, not in CRM fields. Opt-in and notice version are stored with the contact. Message bodies are deleted after the facility's retention period. Model calls run under enterprise terms without training on the data, and staff access is role-based.

What we deliver

  • Intent and routing map approved by the clinical lead
  • Approved FAQ, rate card and test-master knowledge base with named owners
  • Staffed handoff queue with response-time alerts
  • Weekly routing quality report

How we measure it

  • First response time
  • Enquiries resolved without staff
  • Handoff rate for clinical messages
  • Enquiry-to-booking conversion

Book and prepareStandard4–6 weeks

WhatsApp appointment booking, reminders and rescheduling

Patients book consultations and health check-ups on WhatsApp against live HIS or EMR slots, receive approved reminders with preparation notes, and confirm, reschedule or cancel in one tap. Released slots go back to the diary and to the waitlist.

Multi-specialty hospitals · Clinics & day-care centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Phone booking lines queue at peak hours, patients forget appointments, and those who want to reschedule cannot get through. Slots go unused while others wait, and preparation instructions for check-ups and procedures are missed.

Trigger

An opted-in patient taps Book in WhatsApp or scans a booking QR code, or staff create a booking at the desk or by phone in the HIS.

How it runs

  • Offer department, doctor, date and slot in a WhatsApp Flow, reading availability from the HIS or EMR scheduling API, or from a synced slot table where the system has no API.
  • Write the booking back to the HIS, or queue it for front-office entry where there is no API, and confirm with preparation notes written by the department, such as fasting before a check-up.
  • Send reminder templates at intervals the hospital sets, each with confirm, reschedule and cancel buttons.
  • On reschedule or cancel, release the slot in the HIS and offer it to waitlisted patients in order of request.
  • When a consultant's clinic is delayed or canceled, notify booked patients with an approved template once the OPD coordinator approves the message.
  • Report bookings, confirmations, reschedules and no-shows by department and doctor.

Human checkpoint

Front-office staff handle anything outside the booking rules, such as priority appointments or patients who reply with symptoms, which go to the duty nurse. The OPD coordinator approves every delay or cancellation message before it is sent.

Tools

WBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8nSSupabaseRRetoolMPMicrosoft Power BI

Systems it connects

  • Doctor roster
  • Health check-up package master

Data & consent

Name, phone, department, doctor and slot only; templates never state a diagnosis or reason for visit. Opt-in records hold the purposes the patient chose. Bookings stay in the HIS; the automation keeps delivery logs for the agreed retention period, at least one year in line with the DPDP Rules on processing logs.

What we deliver

  • HIS scheduling integration with test evidence
  • Waitlist and slot-release logic
  • No-show and utilization dashboard by department

  • Reschedules made before the slot
  • Slot utilization

Book and prepareStandard4–6 weeks

Home sample collection scheduling and phlebotomist routing

Collection requests from WhatsApp, the website or the call center are checked for serviceable pincodes, booked into slots, batched into phlebotomist routes and tracked through to barcode handover at the lab.

Diagnostics & pathology labs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Collection bookings arrive through several channels and coordinators plan routes by hand each morning. Patients are unsure when the phlebotomist will arrive or whether they should fast, and late or missed visits lead to repeat collections and unhappy referring doctors.

Trigger

A patient requests a home collection, or a referring doctor's order marked for home collection is entered in the LIS.

How it runs

  • Capture address, pincode, preferred window and test list through a WhatsApp Flow or web form, with any prescription image uploaded through a secure link rather than as a chat attachment.
  • Check serviceability and slot capacity, hold the slot and confirm with fasting and preparation notes from the lab's test master.
  • Queue the request for a coordinator to confirm the test list against the prescription before the visit.
  • Batch confirmed visits into routes by area and assign phlebotomists in the scheduling board.
  • Send day-of updates with the phlebotomist's name and arrival window; a delay triggers a revised window and a coordinator alert.
  • Record barcode scans at collection and at lab receipt, and flag samples that miss the transport window set by the lab.

Human checkpoint

The collection coordinator confirms every test list against the prescription and resolves special preparation questions with the lab's medical officer. The phlebotomist verifies the patient's identity on site before collecting.

Book and prepareAdvanced5–7 weeks

Prescription order intake with pharmacist verification

Orders from the pharmacy's app, website or counter scan land in one verification queue. AI extracts medicine lines from the prescription image as a draft, and a registered pharmacist checks every line against the original before anything is billed or dispensed.

Pharmacies & medical retail

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Prescription images arrive blurred, handwritten or incomplete, and staff retype them into the POS. Errors and invalid prescriptions are caught late, and records for Schedule H1 and X medicines must be complete for inspection.

Trigger

A customer uploads a prescription in the pharmacy app or website, or counter staff scan a paper prescription.

How it runs

  • Store the image against the order and extract prescriber, date, patient name, medicine lines and quantities as a draft with confidence scores.
  • Match draft lines to the POS item master without suggesting substitutes, and check stock at the chosen branch.
  • Show the original image and the draft side by side in the pharmacist queue, highlighting unreadable lines and Schedule H1 or X items.
  • The pharmacist checks validity, corrects lines or rejects the order, with the reason sent to the customer.
  • Approved orders move to billing with the prescription reference, and Schedule H1 items prompt the separate register entry in the POS.
  • Send order status through the pharmacy app or SMS, with a route to speak to a pharmacist.

Human checkpoint

A registered pharmacist verifies every prescription and every line before billing or dispensing, and decides when the original prescription must be seen at pickup or delivery. Schedule X items need the original prescription at the counter and are never confirmed remotely.

They are stored in the pharmacy's own systems with role-based access, kept as the drug rules and the pharmacy's policy require, and sent to the extraction model under enterprise terms without training use. None of it passes through WhatsApp.

Arrive and registerStandard4–5 weeks

OPD pre-registration, ABHA Scan and Share and token updates

Patients pre-register before they arrive, can use ABHA Scan and Share where the facility participates, and receive their token and queue position on WhatsApp, so they can wait outside a crowded hall and return when called.

Multi-specialty hospitals · Clinics & day-care centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Morning OPD crowds form at registration and outside consulting rooms. Patients cannot tell how long they will wait, staff repeat the same answers, and a consultant held up in surgery means a full hall with no information.

Trigger

A booked patient is due today, or a patient registers at the desk, scans the facility's QR code or completes ABHA Scan and Share.

How it runs

  • Send a pre-registration link in an approved template the evening before, so demographic details reach the HIS ahead of arrival.
  • Where the HIS is ABDM-integrated, offer ABHA Scan and Share at the entrance as an optional route to registration and a token.
  • On token issue, send the token number and a live position link that reads queue status from the HIS or token display system.
  • Send a call-ahead message when the patient is a set number of places away, and a final call when the doctor is ready.
  • If a consultant is delayed, send waiting patients a delay notice approved by the OPD coordinator, with the option to rebook.
  • Flag the desk when a patient misses the final call, instead of skipping them automatically.

Human checkpoint

The OPD coordinator approves delay notices and decides on out-of-turn priority for elderly, pregnant or visibly unwell patients. Triage nurses, not the system, decide clinical priority.

Tools

WBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8nSSupabaseNNext.js

Systems it connects

  • HIS registration and OPD module
  • Token display or queue management system
  • ABHA Scan and Share through the ABDM-integrated HIS

Data & consent

Token number, first name, department and doctor only. ABHA linking is optional for the patient and runs through the ABDM-integrated HIS, not through the automation. Queue position pages show no names and expire at the end of the day.

What we deliver

  • Queue position page and call-ahead templates
  • Delay notice approval step
  • OPD wait dashboard by department and hour

How we measure it

  • Registration time at the desk

  • Share of patients pre-registered

Treatment and admissionStarter2–4 weeks

Recurring session scheduling for dialysis, chemo and physiotherapy

Treatment plans with repeating sessions become scheduled series with chair or machine capacity checked, reminders sent before each session, and missed sessions flagged to the nurse in charge the same day.

Clinics & day-care centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Day-care units manage repeating sessions in paper diaries or spreadsheets. Capacity clashes surface on the day, reminders depend on staff calling patients, and a missed dialysis or chemotherapy session may go unnoticed until the next visit.

Trigger

The treating doctor records a session plan, with frequency and duration, in the EMR or the unit's scheduling sheet.

How it runs

  • Create the session series from the plan and check chair, machine and staff capacity for each date.
  • Propose alternatives for clashes to the unit coordinator instead of moving sessions automatically.
  • Send a reminder template before each session with any preparation notes the unit has written, plus confirm and cannot-attend buttons.
  • When a patient cannot attend or does not arrive, alert the nurse in charge the same day with the patient's contact details.
  • Update the series when the doctor changes the plan, and send the patient the revised schedule.

Human checkpoint

The unit coordinator approves schedule changes. The nurse in charge follows up every missed session and escalates to the treating doctor, who alone decides any change to the treatment plan.

Tools

  • Chair and machine capacity list
  • Nursing roster

Data & consent

Session dates, unit and patient contact details; messages do not name the treatment. Plans stay in the EMR. The schedule in the coordination tool is restricted to unit staff and archived when the series ends, in line with the clinic's retention policy.

What we deliver

  • Session series builder with capacity checks

  • Unit utilization view

Treatment and admissionAdvanced6–8 weeks

Cashless pre-authorization document tracker

Each insured admission or day-care procedure gets a live checklist of the documents its insurer or TPA needs, secure upload links for the family, timers on insurer queries and an alert when discharge authorization is waiting.

Multi-specialty hospitals · Clinics & day-care centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Pre-authorization requests stall on a missing ID, policy card or investigation report, and insurer queries sit in inboxes. IRDAI's 2024 health insurance master circular expects insurers to decide cashless authorization requests within one hour and final discharge authorization within three hours of the hospital's request, so incomplete files are the delay a hospital can fix.

Trigger

An admission or day-care procedure is marked cashless in the HIS, or the TPA desk opens a new pre-authorization case.

How it runs

  • Create the case with the insurer or TPA's document checklist and a request for the treating doctor's estimate and clinical notes.
  • Send the patient or family an approved template with a secure upload link for missing ID and policy documents.
  • Use a model to read uploaded documents and pre-fill policy number, insured name and dates for the TPA executive to verify.
  • Track submission and insurer queries from NHCX status where the hospital is connected, or as the TPA executive logs them from portals and email, with timers and reminders to the TPA desk and treating doctor.
  • At discharge, alert billing and the TPA desk when final authorization is pending beyond the agreed internal window.
  • Report cycle times by insurer, department and query type for the monthly review.

Human checkpoint

The TPA desk executive checks every extracted field and submits the request; the treating doctor writes and signs the clinical justification and answers medical queries. No document goes to an insurer automatically.

  • Insurer and TPA portals

Data & consent

Upload links expire, and masked Aadhaar copies are requested where the insurer accepts them. Extraction runs under enterprise model terms with no training use, and retention follows the hospital's insurance record policy.

Treatment and admissionAdvanced5–7 weeks

Bed availability, admission and shift-coverage alerts

Admission requests, discharge orders, housekeeping turnaround and shift gaps flow into one internal channel with clear owners, so bed managers and nursing in-charges act on the same live picture instead of phone relays.

Multi-specialty hospitals

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Bed status lives in the HIS, housekeeping works from phone calls, and nursing in-charges juggle absences by phone. Emergency and OPD admissions wait for beds that are free but not yet cleaned, and uncovered shifts are discovered at handover.

Trigger

An admission request, discharge order or bed status change in the HIS ADT module, or a leave or shift swap request in the roster.

How it runs

  • Post each admission request with bed type and isolation needs to the admissions channel, with the bed manager as owner.
  • On a discharge order, create a housekeeping task for that bed and track it to ready status.
  • Escalate to the housekeeping supervisor and bed manager when turnaround passes the agreed window.
  • Notify the contact the patient named, with an approved template, when a bed is allocated, including ward and visiting rules.
  • Route shift swap and leave requests to the nursing in-charge for approval, and flag shifts that fall below the agreed staffing plan.
  • Show a live bed and shift board to the nursing superintendent and the admissions head.

Human checkpoint

The bed manager allocates beds and doctors decide clinical priority between waiting patients. The nursing in-charge approves every swap and decides how to cover a gap. Alerts inform these people; they never assign beds or staff on their own.

Results and reportsStandard4–6 weeks

Consented lab and radiology report delivery

Once a pathologist or radiologist authorizes a report, the patient receives a notification with a secure, expiring link, and the referring doctor gets a copy only where the patient agreed. Reports are linked to ABHA where the lab participates in ABDM.

Diagnostics & pathology labs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Patients call to ask whether reports are ready, staff forward PDFs from personal phones, and nobody can show who received a report. Forwarded attachments also carry health data into chats the lab cannot control.

Trigger

A report's status changes to authorized in the LIS or RIS.

How it runs

  • Check the patient's delivery preference and consent for patient and referring-doctor copies.
  • Send an approved template saying the report is ready, with a secure link that asks for a one-time code sent to the registered mobile number before opening.
  • Send one reminder if the link is not opened within the lab's chosen window, and offer collection or email as alternatives.
  • Deliver the referring doctor's copy to their preferred channel where the patient has agreed.
  • Where the lab is ABDM-integrated, trigger the LIS to link the report to the patient's ABHA for consented sharing.
  • Log every delivery, open and failure for audit and for the lab's turnaround reporting.

Human checkpoint

Only reports authorized by a pathologist or radiologist are released, and the automation never explains results. Questions about a result go to the lab's medical staff or the referring doctor, and critical values follow the escalation path before any notification.

Results and reportsStandard3–5 weeks

Critical result escalation with recorded read-back

When the LIS flags a result outside the lab's approved critical limits, the on-duty pathologist is paged at once, phones the responsible clinician and records the read-back. Unacknowledged alerts climb an agreed escalation ladder.

Diagnostics & pathology labs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Critical values depend on someone noticing a flag and reaching the right clinician by phone, often at night. Calls are not always recorded consistently, while accreditation assessors expect a documented procedure and evidence of who was told and when.

Trigger

The LIS marks a result as critical against the lab's approved critical value list.

How it runs

  • Open an escalation case with lab ID, test, value, sample time and the referring or treating clinician's contact details.
  • Page the on-duty pathologist or senior technologist through the lab's internal channel and a DLT-registered SMS template.
  • The pathologist verifies the result and phones the clinician, or the patient where there is no referring clinician, then records who received it, the time and the read-back.
  • If the case is not acknowledged within the window set in the lab's procedure, escalate to the backup pathologist and then the lab director.
  • Report notification times and incomplete records each week to the quality manager.

Human checkpoint

A pathologist or senior technologist verifies every critical result and speaks personally to the clinician, or to the patient when there is no referring clinician. The automation never puts critical values in messages or interprets them; it pages people and keeps the record.

Discharge and continuing careStandard4–6 weeks

Discharge summary sharing and post-discharge follow-up

When the consultant signs the discharge summary, the patient receives a secure link, follow-up reminders and structured check-ins on the days the care team chose. Any reported concern goes to a care coordinator nurse, never to an automated reply.

Multi-specialty hospitals · Clinics & day-care centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Patients leave with paper summaries and verbal instructions, follow-up visits are missed, and early warning signs are reported late or at another facility. Care teams have no simple way to check in with every discharged patient.

Trigger

The treating consultant signs the discharge summary in the HIS or EMR.

How it runs

  • Send an approved template with a secure, expiring link to the signed discharge summary to the patient or a family member the patient names, alongside the printed copy.
  • Schedule the follow-up appointment reminder and the check-in days the care team recorded in the discharge plan.
  • Ask check-in questions written by the clinical team, such as whether the patient has a concern to discuss, with yes and no buttons.
  • Route any yes, free-text concern or missed check-in to the care coordinator nurse's queue with a short summary of the conversation.
  • State in every message how to reach emergency care, and answer emergency words with the hospital's emergency number and 112.
  • Book the follow-up visit in the HIS and report check-in completion by department.

Human checkpoint

A care coordinator nurse reviews every flagged reply and calls the patient, and the treating doctor decides any change to medicines or care. AI only summarizes free-text replies for the nurse and never advises the patient.

Discharge and continuing careStandard3–5 weeks

Refill-due reminders with pharmacist checks

Chronic patients who opt in receive a reminder when a refill may be due, calculated from the quantity and directions the pharmacist recorded. Every reorder still needs a valid prescription and a pharmacist's verification.

Pharmacies & medical retail

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Patients on long-term medicines run out, travel to a store that is out of stock, or delay their next prescription. Promotional-style reminders for prescription medicines also risk breaching drug rules and messaging platform policies.

Trigger

A dispensing record entered by the pharmacist reaches its estimated refill window for a customer who opted in to reminders.

How it runs

  • Calculate the refill window from the dispensed quantity and the directions recorded at dispensing, never from AI inference.
  • Check stock of the item at the customer's usual branch and hold it for a set period where stock is low.
  • Send a reminder by DLT-registered service SMS, email or app notification that names the store, not the medicine, notes that a valid prescription is needed and carries no offers, which would make it promotional.
  • When the customer responds, open a reorder in the verification queue so a pharmacist checks the prescription's validity and quantity before billing.
  • Stop reminders at once on opt-out, on a pharmacist's note that therapy has changed, or when the prescription has expired.

Human checkpoint

The pharmacist verifies the prescription for every reorder and can pause reminders for any customer. Nothing is dispensed on the strength of a reminder, and dose questions go to the pharmacist or the prescribing doctor.

Feedback and relationshipsStarter2–4 weeks

Patient feedback and service recovery

A short feedback request follows each visit, discharge, report or pharmacy order. Low scores and complaints open tickets with owners and deadlines, possible clinical concerns go to the quality team, and themes are reviewed every week.

Multi-specialty hospitals · Diagnostics & pathology labs · Pharmacies & medical retail

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Feedback is collected on paper or not at all, complaints surface first in public reviews, and nobody tracks whether an unhappy patient was called back. Clinical concerns hidden in feedback comments can go unseen.

Trigger

A visit is closed, a patient is discharged, a report is delivered or a pharmacy order is completed.

How it runs

  • Send one feedback request per episode, with a rating and optional comment, on the channel the patient opted into: WhatsApp for hospitals and labs, SMS or email for pharmacy orders.
  • Classify comments by theme, such as waiting, billing, staff behavior, cleanliness or possible clinical concern, using a model whose labels staff review.
  • Open a service recovery ticket for low ratings and complaints, assigned to the patient relations or store manager with a call-back deadline.
  • Send possible clinical concerns to the quality manager or medical superintendent under the facility's grievance procedure.
  • Close tickets only with a recorded outcome, and send weekly theme and closure reports to department heads.

Human checkpoint

Patient relations staff or the store manager call every low-score patient, and the quality team or medical superintendent reviews any comment that may describe a clinical problem. Model theme labels are checked during the weekly review.

Feedback and relationshipsStarter3–4 weeks

Referring-doctor relationship CRM

Each referring doctor and clinic gets a CRM record of report preferences, turnaround issues, open tickets and service reviews, so relationship managers fix problems early. The CRM has no fields for referral payments, which medical ethics rules prohibit.

Diagnostics & pathology labs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Labs depend on doctors who refer patients and samples, yet relationship managers work from memory and call logs. Turnaround complaints and delivery failures surface late, and informal arrangements can drift towards referral incentives that the NMC ethics regulations prohibit for doctors.

Trigger

A new referring doctor appears in LIS orders, a doctor raises an issue, or a monthly service review is due.

How it runs

  • Create or update the doctor's CRM record from LIS referral fields, with the registration number checked against the medical council register or Healthcare Professionals Registry, and the preferred report channel.
  • Log turnaround delays, report errors and delivery failures for that doctor's patients as linked issues with owners and due dates.
  • Alert the relationship manager when issues repeat for a doctor or pass their due date.
  • Prepare a monthly service summary per doctor with aggregated volumes and open issues for the relationship manager.
  • Leave out any field or workflow for commissions, gifts or fee sharing in the CRM configuration.

Human checkpoint

The relationship manager owns each doctor record and decides on follow-up, and the lab director reviews the monthly summaries. Commercial terms with hospitals and institutions are handled by management outside the automation, under the lab's ethics policy.

Tools

  • Referring doctor directory

Data & consent

Holds doctors' professional contact details and aggregated referral counts; patient-level data stays in the LIS. Report copies are sent by the report delivery workflow only with the patient's recorded consent. CRM access is limited to the relationship team and lab leadership.

What we deliver

  • Referring doctor CRM model without incentive fields
  • LIS referral sync
  • Issue tracking linked to doctor records
  • Monthly service summary dashboard

How we measure it

  • Turnaround complaints per month
  • Report copy delivery failures
  • Doctors reviewed each month
